The `studioThemesMap` is created on every component instantiation. Since `studioThemes` is a static constant imported from `$lib/core/meechie-studio`, this map should ideally be defined once in that module and exported. This would avoid redundant object allocations and processing every time the page is mounted, which aligns better with the 'memory optimization' goal of this PR.

`languageOptions.globals` currently merges both `globals.browser` and `globals.node` for *all* files. This makes `no-undef` much less effective (e.g., browser-only globals like `window/localStorage` won’t be flagged in Node-only scripts/tests, and Node globals like `process` won’t be flagged in client code). Consider scoping globals by file patterns (e.g. `**/*.svelte` / client TS gets `globals.browser`, while `scripts/**`, `probes/**`, `tests/**`, `playwright.config.ts`, etc. get `globals.node`).

The config disables `no-unused-vars` globally. That will hide real issues across the whole repo (including non-Svelte files) and makes linting significantly less useful. If the goal is to avoid false positives in Svelte/components, prefer limiting this to `**/*.svelte` (or configure ignore patterns for unused args/vars) rather than turning the rule off everywhere.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Re-enable unused-variable checks globally**

Turning `no-unused-vars` off at the root config disables a key safety check for every JS/TS/Svelte file, so newly introduced dead variables and typo-driven logic mistakes will silently pass lint. This is a maintainability regression introduced by this commit; if the intent was to suppress specific false positives (for example optional `catch` bindings), the rule should stay enabled globally and be narrowed with targeted overrides instead.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Split browser and node globals into scoped overrides**

Defining both `globals.browser` and `globals.node` at the root makes ESLint treat Node and browser-only symbols as always defined in every file, which hides server/client boundary mistakes (for example, accidental `process` usage in client Svelte code or `window` usage in server modules) that would otherwise be caught by `no-undef` before runtime. Scope these globals by file pattern or runtime instead of enabling both globally.
